engineUnchanged: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.

One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Initial area targets are a snapshot at resolution, with no selective omission or later entry damage. Each affected creature uses its own save/defenses; a shared raw damage roll is not a shared defensive result. No Burning, Frozen, Deafened, Poisoned or other unnamed condition arises merely from the damage type. sourceCardUnchanged.name: Detect Weather

operational.targets: One point you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect, on your current plane.
operational.duration: Instantaneous information about the following 24 hours; no continuing buff or concentration.
operational.resolution: No roll. The Director gives an accurate 24-hour forecast for the local outdoor region within 1 mile horizontally of that point on the same plane. Describe meaningful local variations when the terrain makes the region's weather differ. An indoor or underground point refers to the outdoor local weather above/around that same geographical location rather than the room's climate.
operational.effect: Report relevant temperature bands/trends, precipitation type and approximate timing, wind direction/strength, weather-caused visibility and significant storm or environmental-weather hazards. The report is intelligible to the caster and accurate for the current natural processes and already-existing magical weather expected to continue; record the forecast as the current weather expectation. A weatherless environment reports that fact. It supplies useful specific conditions rather than a vague warning that weather might change.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in targets, range, duration or information.
operational.limitations: A genuinely new later cause, such as a voluntary weather-changing spell, new supernatural event or catastrophe, can change actual conditions after the forecast without having been predicted. The Director must identify an actual intervening cause in the game record, not silently invalidate the forecast by rerolling unchanged weather; this need not reveal that cause to the caster. The spell does not control weather, grant exposure protection, reveal encounters/loot, complete travel, recover resources or predict unrelated events. Information about a specifically protected subject remains limited by that actual protection; ordinary ambient weather is not automatically protected by a creature standing in it. Actual class access and repertoire, audible V/free-hand S components, casting sequence, Refrain/Dissonance, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base RP is 0 but repeated cantrips still follow their actual strain rules. No automatic upcast or unstated scaling. Source-specific protections apply only to their actual scope. Protection from Scrying prevents new Divination/Scrying information about its protected subject, including beneficial inspection, but grants no blanket immunity to damage, buffs or other noninformational mechanics merely because of their school; it does not erase already-known facts or ordinary records.

source.originalText: Arcane Lock: Create a magical barrier that prevents entry or access to an object or area.

4.name: Analyze Magic
4.rangeAndTarget: One magical creature, object or effect within 30 feet
4.effect: Analyze Magic. Tags: base, active, wizard-spell, divination, knowledge. Make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + the effect's spell rank, treating a non-spell effect's Director-assigned tier as rank. On success learn its school or magical category, one active mechanical property and whether it is currently sustained, cursed or bound to another effect. Failure reveals only that magic is present.

source.originalText: Analyze Magic: Study a magical effect or item to gain insight into its properties and function.

5.name: Dispel Magic
5.rangeAndTarget: One creature, object or magical effect within 60 feet
5.effect: Dispel Magic. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, abjuration. Choose one ongoing spell effect you can perceive. If its rank is 3 or lower, end it. If it is rank 4 or higher, make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + spell rank; success ends it. Permanent artifact properties and effects explicitly immune to dispelling are unaffected.

source.originalText: Dispel Magic: End magical effects in an area or on a target.

6.name: Spellbook Study
6.effect: Spellbook Study. Tags: base, active, matrix, ritual. Replace one currently prepared matrix with one legal spell recorded in your spellbook. The replacement must be within your Wizard rank limit. This is the normal midday substitution permission; it does not alter the spellbook, create another prepared-matrix position or reset first-cast/Refrain history for an underlying matrix family already cast this encounter.

source.originalText: Spellbook Study: Spend time studying your spellbook to prepare a different selection of spells.

7.name: Dimensional Pocket
7.effect: Dimensional Pocket. Tags: arch, active, wizard-spell, conjuration, ritual. Create an extradimensional storage space holding up to 100 pounds or 10 cubic feet of unattended nonliving material. Retrieving or placing an item while adjacent to the opening uses an object interaction. Living creatures cannot enter. When duration ends, remaining contents appear harmlessly in the nearest unoccupied space.

source.originalText: Dimensional Pocket: Create a small extradimensional space to store items.

8.name: Matrix Efficiency
8.effect: Matrix Efficiency. Tags: base, passive, matrix. Your normal full daily Spell Matrix preparation time is reduced from 1 hour to 45 minutes. This does not reduce the separate 10-minute midday substitution ritual, spell scribing, rituals or spellbook reconstruction unless another feature explicitly says so.

source.originalText: Matrix Efficiency: Reduce the preparation time for spells by 25%.

9.name: Sigil Rewrite
9.effect: Sigil Rewrite. Tags: arch, passive-upgrade, matrix. Replace one prepared matrix with a different spell from your spellbook of exactly the same rank without performing the normal 10-minute ritual. The replacement receives no special Dissonance reset for a matrix family already used this encounter and must obey current Wizard rank eligibility.

source.originalText: Sigil Rewrite: Once/day, instantly swap a spell you know for another of the same tier

10.name: Spell Preservation
10.effect: Spell Preservation. Tags: hero, spellbinder, passive, spellbook. Your primary spellbook cannot be destroyed, erased or rendered permanently unreadable by non-artifact mundane or magical means. It can still be stolen, hidden, transported, suppressed, sealed by an artifact-level effect or voluntarily abandoned. Copies and backup books do not automatically receive this protection.

source.originalText: Spell Preservation: Your spellbook cannot be destroyed by non-artifact means.

10.name: Runic Snare
10.effect: Runic Snare. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, glyph, control. Place a visible-to-you glyph. The first hostile creature entering the square makes a Dexterity save. Failure deals S d6 force damage, causes Restrained until the end of its next turn and makes it drop one non-attuned held item of its choice. Success takes half damage with no restraint or drop. A Restrained target may repeat a Strength save at the end of its turn.

source.originalText: Runic Snare: Glyph trap explodes in a 2x2 root + disarm on trigger

11.name: Floating Preparation
11.effect: Floating Preparation. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. Increase your maximum prepared Spell Matrix count by 1. The extra matrix can come from any school and obeys all ordinary spellbook and rank restrictions. It is a prepared matrix for every rule, including protected strain, duplicate-family tracking and Matrix Mastery modifications.

source.originalText: Floating Preparation: Prepare 1 extra spell from any school each day

12.name: Counterpulse
12.rangeAndTarget: Caster whose spell you successfully Counterspelled
12.duration: Until end of target's next turn
12.effect: Counterpulse. Tags: hero, spellbinder, counter, control. Immediately after your Counterspell succeeds, spend 1 RP. The countered caster is Silenced until the end of its next turn. This is part of the successful counter event rather than another spell cast and cannot trigger another Counterpulse.

source.originalText: Counterpulse: Countering a spell silences the caster for 1 round

13.name: Matrix Mastery
13.effect: Matrix Mastery. Tags: arch, passive, matrix. During preparation you may assign at most one common Matrix Mastery modification to each ordinary prepared spell: Quick Substitution, Component Enhancement, Matrix Linking or Stability Reinforcement, using the exact common definitions in the Wizard engine. Always-prepared class-card matrices cannot receive these modifications unless a card explicitly says otherwise.

source.originalText: Matrix Mastery: Modify spell matrices to change minor aspects of prepared spells.

14.name: Spell Absorption
14.rangeAndTarget: One hostile spell that directly targets you
14.effect: Spell Absorption. Tags: hero, spellbinder, wizard-spell, abjuration. Trigger after you become the target of a hostile spell but before it resolves. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell rank. On success that spell has no effect on you, though it resolves normally against other targets, and you gain temporary HP equal to spell rank + M. On failure it resolves normally and the use is spent.

source.originalText: Spell Absorption: Absorb a hostile spell, gaining temporary hit points equal to the spell's level.

15.name: Improved Concentration
15.effect: Improved Concentration. Tags: arch, passive, concentration. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made because damage threatens your concentration on a Wizard spell. This does not alter the DC, protect a Tether from rules that explicitly end both effects, or prevent Silence, incapacitation and other non-damage concentration failures.

source.originalText: Improved Concentration: Advantage on concentration checks when taking damage.

automaticCards.name: Arcane Tradition
automaticCards.frequency: Automatic at Wizard 3; not a selection
automaticCards.effect: Arcane Tradition. Tags: arch, school, automatic. Your level-1 Arcane School becomes your Arcanist tradition; do not choose a second school. Prepare one additional matrix from that same school each day without counting it against your normal prepared-matrix maximum. It otherwise obeys all ordinary rank, spellbook, Dissonance and duplicate-family rules.

source.originalText: Arcane Tradition: Choose a school of magic to specialize in, gaining bonuses to spells of that school.

automaticCards.name: Counterspell
automaticCards.cost: 3 RP
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One creature you perceive casting a spell within 60 feet
automaticCards.effect: Counterspell. Tags: arch-source, automatic, wizard-spell, abjuration, disruption. Trigger when a creature begins casting a spell. Make an Intelligence check adding proficiency against DC 10 + twice the spell's rank, treating rank 0 as 0. Success negates the triggering spell after its costs are paid; failure lets it resolve. This is gained automatically at Wizard 2 and is never also selected from the Arch pool.

source.originalText: Counterspell: Disrupt an enemy's spellcasting, potentially negating their spell entirely.

automaticCards.name: Ritual Casting
automaticCards.cost: 0 RP unless the individual ritual explicitly states otherwise
automaticCards.frequency: At will outside encounters with sufficient time
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5184. Cast a Wizard spell bearing the Ritual tag directly from your spellbook without preparing it. Increase its casting time by at least 10 minutes. Ritual Casting cannot be completed during an encounter, does not use an ordinary prepared-matrix position and does not generate or vent normal casting Dissonance.

source.originalText: | 2 | Counterspell Reaction, Ritual Casting |

automaticCards.name: School Mastery
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5186. This is the one School Mastery progression grant, not a second school choice or duplicate feat. Increase the level-1 Arcane School spell-attack and spell-save bonus from +1 to +2 total. Its school passive and bonus-spell rules otherwise remain unchanged.

source.originalText: | 5 | Bonus Feat: School Mastery |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Ward
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5187. After preparing spells, choose one of acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder that is dealt by at least one prepared spell of your Arcane School. Gain resistance to that damage type until your next long rest. If none of your prepared school spells deals a damage type, choose force. This is provisional completion of the source's ambiguous 'chosen school's element' wording.

source.originalText: | 6 | Arcane Ward (resistance to chosen school's element) |

automaticCards.name: Dual Cast
automaticCards.cost: Pay the complete RP costs of both spells
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5188. Choose two DIFFERENT prepared Wizard spells of rank 1 or 2, neither of which summons a creature or grants an additional Action. Cast both sequentially as one Action, paying both RP costs. They cannot both require concentration. Each matrix separately updates first-cast/Refrain history. Features that trigger merely from 'casting a spell' may trigger once for each actual matrix unless that feature itself says once per turn; no trigger may create another Dual Cast or additional full Action.

source.originalText: | 9 | Dual Cast (cast 2 Tier 1–2 spells in a round) |

automaticCards.name: Overchannel
automaticCards.cost: Pay the Core V 2 RP cost for one rank above the spell's normal cast rank
automaticCards.rangeAndTarget: One prepared spell you are beginning to cast
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5190. Cast one prepared spell as though it were one rank higher than the highest rank at which you could normally cast that SAME spell, provided the spell has an explicit higher-rank scaling rule. Overchannel does not teach or prepare a higher-rank spell, cannot exceed effective rank 9 and cannot be combined with another generic Overcast rule during this pilot. All normal Dissonance/Refrain rules still apply.

source.originalText: | 13 | Overchannel (cast a spell 1 tier higher once/day) |

automaticCards.name: Arcane Feedback
automaticCards.effect: Source progression line 5191, converted from historical slot wording to RP. After your Counterspell successfully negates a spell, restore 1 RP, never above your normal maximum. A counter produced by a companion, reflected spell or copied Counterspell does not trigger this feature.

source.originalText: | 15 | Arcane Feedback (after successfully countering a spell, recover 1 RP once per round) |

engineUnchanged: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.

sourceCardUnchanged.name: Warding Bond

operational.targets: One willing ally other than yourself, perceived within range and line of effect. Neither participant may already participate in another Warding Bond, as caster or protected ally.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; retain that virtual marker through initiative changes, departure or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier when concentration ends. Also ends if either participant dies. Reaching 0 HP alone is not a separate ending condition; ordinary Incapacitated/concentration rules still apply.
operational.resolution: Automatic on legal casting. On each eligible positive incoming damage packet to the ally, apply the mandatory post-defense transfer described below; a rounded-zero transfer claims no transfer operation.
operational.effect: The ally gains +1 AC and +1 to saves, subject separately to the strongest applicable flat bonus. After the ally's defenses and legal prevention, before temporary HP, transfer floor(remaining damage / 2) to you and leave the remainder on the ally. Keep the damage type. Your transferred share skips a second mitigation/prevention stage and cannot transfer again; apply your temporary HP, HP, applicable life-state protections, Wounds and concentration consequences normally. The ally retains the hit, failed-save, critical and attached-rider identity; you were not hit and did not fail that save merely because damage transferred.
operational.scaling: None. The rank-2 duplicate grants no upgrade or extra effect.
operational.limitations: Use DAMAGE_SHARING_PLAYTEST.md: one transfer operation per original-recipient damage root, across all owners. A prior pre-mitigation split preempts this transfer; competing positive mandatory post-defense claims are chosen by the original target. The retained ally portion cannot subsequently be transferred again after this split. Complete the current packet's split and life consequences before concentration failure caused by that packet ends the bond; never undo a committed share. One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Initial range/line of effect are required, but no continuing distance or line-of-effect tether is imposed. This ordinary spell neither consumes nor increases the Paladin class redirection round ledger and grants none of its named healing/resource riders or proc permissions. Unrelated downstream triggers still require their own exact source authorization. Direct HP payments are not damage and cannot be transferred. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 30 feet, concentration 1 minute, +1 AC/saves and half-damage sharing; M/F uses focus. NEW: willing ally, conserved mandatory post-defense split, rounding, participation and life endpoints, no continued tether and ordinary-spell/class-engine separation. CONFLICT RULING: source-derived class access is rank 1; duplicate rank-2 block is retained as evidence only.

sourceCardUnchanged.name: Thunderwave

operational.targets: A10-foot cone originating from you in a chosen direction. Affect every creature whose actual occupied space is in the cone with line of effect from its origin, including allies. Being the origin alone does not include or self-push you.
operational.duration: Instantaneous, no concentration.
operational.resolution: Each affected creature makes a Strength save. Roll2d8 thunder once. Failure: full raw damage and independently attempt the mandatory10-foot outward push. Success: half the raw damage rounded down and no push. Apply damage and movement defenses in their own scopes.
operational.effect: On a failed save, force the creature directly radially away from the cone origin toward a total10-foot displacement, stopping early only when ordinary forced-movement legality prevents further movement: an obstacle, illegal occupied destination, geometry or applicable defense. Neither caster nor target chooses an arbitrarily shorter open path. A thunder packet reduced to0 does not prevent the independent failed-save push. Existing support, hazard and falling procedures apply if legal displacement carries the target beyond an edge.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, targets, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: No extra collision/impact damage, unprinted object fling, building destruction, Deafened or arbitrary-direction movement. The push itself supplies no new falling clock or general forced-movement immunity. Source-defined geometric eligibility still controls; the caster is not forced away from itself merely because it is the origin. Initial area targets are a snapshot at resolution, with no selective omission or later entry damage. Each affected creature uses its own save/defenses; a shared raw damage roll is not a shared defensive result. No Burning, Frozen, Deafened, Poisoned or other unnamed condition arises merely from the damage type. Actual class/source access, repertoire, level, action availability, components, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and cast/counter/outcome hooks follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. These actual rank-1 placements have base 2 RP; real source modifiers and strain surcharges still apply. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable free hand or an actual exception, and F is the ordinary class focus. A legal cast commits payment and cast-begin consequences before its Counterspell window; later failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. Spell attacks use d20 + PB + actual casting modifier against AC; natural 1 misses/natural 20 hits and doubles only actual attack damage dice. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. Actual target/area defenses and source-specific hooks retain their real trigger scopes. No automatic level scaling, generic upcast, new action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action,10-foot source range,V/S/F,2d8 thunder and10-foot push. sourceCardUnchanged.name: Shatter

operational.targets: Choose a perceived point within 10 feet and line of effect. The initial area is a 10-foot-radius sphere around it. After interruption but before any damage, fix one snapshot of all eligible creatures, ordinary nonmagical discrete objects and bounded structural sections within the sphere with center line of effect.
operational.duration: Instantaneous, no concentration; actual damaged objects retain ordinary damage consequences.
operational.resolution: Roll one shared 3d8 thunder base and one shared additional 1d8 thunder object bonus. Each affected creature makes a Constitution save: failure takes the base; success takes half the base, rounded down. Creatures never receive the object bonus. Each eligible object or selected structural section takes base plus bonus as ONE grouped thunder packet, without a save, using its actual durability/material/damage defenses. Apply recipient defenses independently; do not turn the four damage dice into separate packets.
operational.effect: Eligible objects are ordinary nonmagical objects that are unattended, caster-held, or deliberately offered/exposed by willing holders; hostile worn/carried inventory is not automatically included. For each actual distinct large structural whole or terrain feature, select at most one contiguous exposed section wholly within the original sphere and bounded by a 5-foot cube. Use the eligible section containing its line-of-effect-reachable point nearest the spell center. Resolve equivalent nearest-point ties by stable neutral geometry/order fixed before damage, not caster choice or post-damage Director optimization. The Director determines actual structural identity and hidden boundaries without revealing them merely because the spell was cast. Arbitrarily naming bricks/panels/floorboards does not multiply one structure’s packets. A genuinely separate freestanding object remains independent. A large discrete object beyond the damage scale of its actual durability rules receives damage only to its legal affected section, not automatic transfer through the entire object. Fix all recipients and sections before any packet; destroying cover cannot expose new targets or cause another scan. Actual later support/collapse/falling consequences follow their own rules. Initial area recipients are a snapshot at resolution, with no selective omission or later entry damage. Apply the stated geometry and line of effect from the origin/center before damage removes cover; allies and caster are included only when the card actually includes their occupied space. Roll the stated raw area damage once, then apply each recipient’s save and defenses independently. Halved damage rounds down before individual defenses. Distinct recipients retain separate damage packets and callbacks. No attack critical applies to area save damage.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, targets, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: The short 10-foot point range and separate 10-foot radius both apply. No damage extends outside the selected section/sphere, no automatic whole-building collapse or propagation is granted, and no Deafened, construct vulnerability, magic-item suppression or named shattered condition is added. No one can choose a concealed load-bearing element or optimize sections after damage outcomes. Actual class/source access, repertoire, level, action availability, components, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and cast/counter/outcome hooks follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. These actual rank-2 placements have base 3 RP; actual source modifiers and strain surcharges still apply. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable free hand or an actual exception, and F is the ordinary class focus. A legal cast commits payment and cast-begin consequences before its Counterspell window; later failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. Spell attacks use d20 + PB + actual casting modifier against AC; natural 1 misses/natural 20 hits and doubles only actual attack damage dice. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. Actual defenses and source-specific hooks retain their real trigger scopes. No automatic level scaling, generic upcast, new action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 10-foot casting range, V/S/F, 3d8 thunder in 10-foot radius and extra object damage. NEW: perceived point/sphere, CON half for creatures, shared +1d8 for legal nonmagical objects in one grouped packet, fixed pre-damage snapshot and deterministic bounded structural section procedure.

sourceCardUnchanged.name: Detect Weather

operational.targets: One point you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect, on your current plane.
operational.duration: Instantaneous information about the following 24 hours; no continuing buff or concentration.
operational.resolution: No roll. The Director gives an accurate 24-hour forecast for the local outdoor region within 1 mile horizontally of that point on the same plane. Describe meaningful local variations when the terrain makes the region's weather differ. An indoor or underground point refers to the outdoor local weather above/around that same geographical location rather than the room's climate.
operational.effect: Report relevant temperature bands/trends, precipitation type and approximate timing, wind direction/strength, weather-caused visibility and significant storm or environmental-weather hazards. The report is intelligible to the caster and accurate for the current natural processes and already-existing magical weather expected to continue; record the forecast as the current weather expectation. A weatherless environment reports that fact. It supplies useful specific conditions rather than a vague warning that weather might change.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in targets, range, duration or information.
operational.limitations: A genuinely new later cause, such as a voluntary weather-changing spell, new supernatural event or catastrophe, can change actual conditions after the forecast without having been predicted. The Director must identify an actual intervening cause in the game record, not silently invalidate the forecast by rerolling unchanged weather; this need not reveal that cause to the caster. The spell does not control weather, grant exposure protection, reveal encounters/loot, complete travel, recover resources or predict unrelated events. Information about a specifically protected subject remains limited by that actual protection; ordinary ambient weather is not automatically protected by a creature standing in it. Actual class access and repertoire, audible V/free-hand S components, casting sequence, Refrain/Dissonance, class hooks and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base RP is 0 but repeated cantrips still follow their actual strain rules. No automatic upcast or unstated scaling. Source-specific protections apply only to their actual scope. Protection from Scrying prevents new Divination/Scrying information about its protected subject, including beneficial inspection, but grants no blanket immunity to damage, buffs or other noninformational mechanics merely because of their school; it does not erase already-known facts or ordinary records.

engineUnchanged: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.
